operations.read: key (32), value 0: 128 bytes back (amount, account, signer, exit address), each a word
operations.bond: key (32) with value: a fresh key records the origin as the account AND the exit address; a bonded key accepts more from its account only; the amount after must be within the cap
operations.bond_with_exit: key (32) || exit (32, the address right-aligned) with value: the bond with its exit address set in the bond transaction (a fresh key), or, by the account, a change of the exit address with the top-up (the lock is NOT modelled on the lab build: the exit changes at once)
operations.set_signer: key (32) || signer (32, an Ed25519 public key), value 0, by the account
operations.claim_lab: the STAND-IN on the lab build: sk (32) || to (32, the address right-aligned) || zero (32), value 0, by anyone presenting the secret: pk = G(sk) must be bonded; the whole amount leaves at once and the key is unbonded; to equal to the exit address pays everything (the holder's orderly exit); any other to pays less phi = one quarter burnt to the fund; a reveal in a transaction is readable by the sealer that sees it first, which the proof form removes
operations.claim: the form the registry takes when the risc0 verifier is in the node (the protocol team sends the sha): key (32), the claimant's address as a 32-byte word, the share s_0 (32), then the proof pi (the Groth16 wrap per the project's ruling of 10:30 UK; the composite receipt stays in the block body): the key-bound proof of SPEC-R0A 0.9.1 under domain 1 with K 1 over m_0 = BLAKE3(tag("IgneumHash/R0A/hostile") || C || pk || LE64(nonce_b) || to) with C = u64be(chain id), the registry verifying the receipt against PI_IMAGE_ID and the journal u8(1) || LE32(1) || pk || m_0 || s_0; the same payout rule as claim_lab. The bond key is pk = G(sk) = BLAKE3(tag("IgneumHash/R0A/bond-pk") || sk), never an Ed25519 key; the proof is made by pow/pi's pi-claim from the secret's file

authority.ruled: main, 11 Oct 2026 10:30 UK: the claim carries the small Groth16 wrap of the receipt (sub-kilobyte; the hash team defines the per-domain receipt kind in SPEC 0.9.1 and the pi-claim entry points), not the composite receipt (221 KB, over the node's 128 KiB transaction bound); C in the claim message is the chain id as u64 big-endian (7315 here), the vector set's test C only on devnet4's rows, labelled; the protocol team lands this chain with the registry version 3 in these forms with the wrap
